outcome: rate of preterm birth prior to 37 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 422 women treated with progesterone to prevent preterm birth, who delivered in a single university-affiliated tertiary medical-center and were at risk for preterm birth due to prior preterm birth or cervical length below 25 mm, excluding those with significant maternal morbidity, pregnancies achieved by artificial reproductive technique, or cerclage placement.
finding: Different progesterone preparations may possess different efficacy in preventing preterm delivery prior to 37 weeks of gestation, with Endometrin showing the lowest rates of preterm birth.
